# Draft:United Kingdom and Eire Council for Malaysian Students

United Kingdom and Eire Council for Malaysian Students (UKEC) is a student-led umbrella organisation representing Malaysian students in the United Kingdom and Ireland. Founded in 1995, UKEC serves as a coordinating body for Malaysian student societies across universities in both countries. The organisation focuses on supporting student welfare, facilitating professional development, promoting leadership opportunities, and fostering unity among Malaysian students studying abroad.
UKEC works in collaboration with Malaysian student societies, government agencies, academic institutions, and industry partners to organise events and initiatives. These include career fairs, leadership summits, policy discussions, and community engagement programmes. Through these activities, UKEC aims to provide a platform for Malaysian students to connect with one another while maintaining engagement with developments in Malaysia.
History
UKEC was established in 1995 by Malaysian students studying in the United Kingdom and Ireland who sought to create a unified platform to coordinate activities and represent student interests. In its early years, the organisation focused primarily on facilitating communication among Malaysian student societies and organising community-building events.
As the number of Malaysian students in the region grew, UKEC expanded its scope to include professional and leadership development initiatives. The organisation began organising large-scale events such as career fairs and leadership forums, which connected Malaysian students with employers, policymakers, and community leaders. These initiatives aimed to support students’ career pathways and encourage engagement with national issues.
Throughout the 2000s and 2010s, UKEC broadened its activities to include welfare-related initiatives, policy discussions, and partnerships with external organisations. The council also strengthened its structure by introducing specialised portfolios responsible for areas such as careers, welfare, partnerships, and community engagement.
In recent years, UKEC has continued to serve as a platform for collaboration among Malaysian student societies across the United Kingdom and Ireland. Its activities have included leadership summits, career development programmes, and engagement sessions with stakeholders from both Malaysia and the host countries. The organisation remains student-led, with an annually elected council overseeing its initiatives and strategic direction.
